body:
[A10] #649 final summary (side project, measurement only; findings page `docs/findings/649_RESOURCE_MAP_AND_SENSITIVITY.md`, merged in dev `6c22d3ca` via PR #650). Supersedes the round-1 figures posted earlier.

- The shipping 1x1 route at dev `241f9184` (50,767 LUT) splits into the protocol processor 23,904 (47.1 %), the rest of
  `milan_datapath` 18,296 (36.0 %) and the SoC side 8,567 (16.9 %). Every one of its 175 blocks has its LUT, FF, RAMB
  and DSP figures read from both the utilization report and the placed-cell census, and the totals are tied to the
  `route-1x1` record. In the rest of the datapath the large blocks are the gPTP plane (5,004) and the CSR block (3,073).
- Each stream per direction costs 3,828 LUT, 2,911 FF and 1.5 BRAM tiles out of context (Vivado, 1x1 to 4x4), two
  thirds of the LUTs in the processor, with a falling cost per added stream (4,739, then 3,464 each). No shape above 1x1
  fits the device.
- Channels per stream and the TDM capture width cost nothing; the TDM render lane is 499 routed LUT.
- The low-function-cost prunes (RX address filter, latency taps, loopback lane, probes) could save up to about 1,200
  routed LUT, a tenth of the 12,727-LUT NFR-RES-01 gap: the gap is redesign territory, the processor first, then the gPTP
  plane and the CSR block.
- SoC options the recipe refuses, priced from a scratch recipe copy (not buildable under the shipping software
  profile): each further core about 1,480 LUT; both L1 caches about 1,200; NaxRiscv about 14,300; no L2 is built on the
  shipping cacheless core. These are synthesized at the default directive, so they compare with the shipping image only
  through the page's calibration factor (1.13 SoC, 1.16 CPU).
- Yosys LUT counts are 2.2 to 2.8 times Vivado's and Yosys does not enforce the RTL's elaboration guards (sv2v turns
  `$error` into `initial $display`); the out-of-context Vivado anchor is within 3.3 % of the route.
- Tooling gaps filed: #651 (Yosys ignores the elaboration guards), #652 (builder accepts 235 names against the 128 NAME block), #654 (`--with-fpu` / `--l2-bytes` silently ignored).

[A10] **Correction of my previous comment.** The owner clarified: Mark II comes **before** P3, not after it. Milestone 12 is now due 2026-12-15, ahead of milestone 6 (Robustness as a gate (P3), due 2026-12-31). The #396 release-gate runs (soak, power-cycle torture and the 72 h zero-glitch audio run) therefore run on the redesigned image. The 2026-10-03 condition "after milestone 10, Instrument verification" no longer applies. The milestone 12 description records this. #640 and #233 leave On Hold for the backlog; the redesign plan comes first.

[A10] **Manager rulings on [A540]'s plan (STOP 5990726992, head `06f5e7e5`), decisions D1, D3, D6, D7 and D8.** D2, D4, D5 and D9 change owner directives or the requirements, so they are put to the owner. Those rulings follow in a separate comment.

- **D1, the equivalence bar: accepted as proposed.** A redesigned engine is equivalent when:
  - it has PDU-level and port-transaction equivalence against the current engine, over each suite's stimulus;
  - every suite and campaign passes at its count;
  - tests that pin a cycle are re-targeted under review, never deleted.
- **D3, internal latency: not protocol-visible, with a bound.** A change of internal latency with no wire change is not a protocol-visible effect when three things hold:
  - each lane states and tests a deterministic upper bound per response path;
  - every normative timeout holds with margin;
  - the bench timing figures hold: stream restart under 1 s (#75), fast connect, and the saved-state capture bound.
- **D6, one engine for gPTP and AECP: deferred** to the week-4 re-measure after M3's first sub-lane routes.
- **D7, re-baseline during Mark II: accepted as proposed.**
  - Mark II lanes record their measured image in the plan's ledger.
  - The resource gate still judges each lane against the last record, so growth stays visible.
  - M9 re-records at the target.
  - `AREA_BUDGET.md` gets the same rule, plus the 2026-10-05 schedule correction (milestone 12 before P3).
- **D8, the margin.** The bar is NFR-RES-01's 38,040 LUT with timing met. My "about 5 %" was a planning margin, not a requirement. The plan aims for at least 1 % under the limit, and the week-4 re-measure decides whether M10 or more is needed.

**Lanes that need no owner decision** can start once #661 (PR #663) merges, so that parent lanes build on the new pin: M2, M5, M6, M7, and M3 (now unblocked by D1 and D3). Vivado runs one at a time under the host lock, so each lane plans its route measurement as one queued job.

The plan document goes to review as a docs PR once the owner's decisions are recorded in it.

[A10] **Owner decisions of 2026-10-05 on the Mark II plan (D2, D4, D5, D9).**

- **D2: no.** The diagnostics stay in the shipping image. The owner needs that information. L6, about 700 LUT, is dropped from the plan.
- **D4: yes.** DDR3 is dropped for on-chip main memory (L11a). Long term, no DDR3 will be available. #70's saved-state staging buffers are resized to the shape's container size, and the SoC memory map changes. This supersedes the earlier "DDR3 for the control path" directive.
- **D5: yes, conditionally.** The control core becomes a smaller cacheless RV32I (L11b). The condition is that the saved-state capture bound (8x8 at most 24.5 ms, `check_nvm_capture.py`) measures fine on the smaller core, with boot timing held. Otherwise the change is reverted.
- **D9: no for Mark II.** Moving slow-path control to the RISC-V (L2) stays a later option and is not planned.

**Effect on the ledger.**
- Without L6, the central estimate for M0 to M8 becomes about 38,268 LUT. That is about 228 over the 38,040 limit.
- With M10 (L10b, one engine for gPTP and AECP), it becomes about 37,068.

So M10 moves from "if needed" to planned, and D6 is decided: one engine for gPTP and AECP is in the plan. The week-4 re-measure after M3's first sub-lane still checks the estimates.

The plan document and `AREA_BUDGET.md` are updated before the plan PR goes to review.

[A10] **Owner clarification of D9, 2026-10-05.** The intent for milestone 13 is a **software-defined, configurable** slow path. Each function (descriptor serving, MAAP, SRP declaration bookkeeping, ACMP state) runs either fully inside the fabric or on the RISC-V, selected by configuration. The fabric-only shape stays supported.

The boundary between fabric and firmware is to be **an elegant CSR register interface**, not a packet-based mailbox. Both placements must present the same wire behaviour. The milestone 13 description is updated to match. It is still not part of milestone 12.

[A10] **Owner decision, 2026-10-05, the milestone 13 interface.** The CSR boundary is withdrawn. ACMP, MAAP and SRP move into the bare-metal software core and exchange frames through **several packet mailboxes**.

The **fabric ingress path filters packets** before the mailboxes, so a busy network cannot flood the core. The software core also **reads the saved entity state from the flash and applies it** (the #70 restore).

The milestone 13 description is updated to match.

[A10] **Owner, 2026-10-05: milestone 13 scope.**
- **ADP moves too,** with ACMP, MAAP and SRP. A dead core then stops advertising. The fabric sends a grandmaster-change event so that ADP re-advertises.
- **The interface must port from the RISC-V soft core to a hard core.** It uses memory-mapped block RAM rings, a doorbell and an interrupt, 32-bit accesses only, and no DMA. Each host gets a bus adapter: Wishbone, or AXI4-Lite and AXI4. Firmware is portable C behind a small HAL. One YAML contract generates the fabric module, the C header and the documentation.

**Expected resources** (routed figures from the dev `e6172750` map in `MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md`; the costs are estimates, to be measured).

Blocks that leave the fabric:

| Block | LUT | FF |
|---|---:|---:|
| SRP | 4,219 | 6,264 |
| ACMP listener | 1,414 | 1,110 |
| ACMP binding store | 790 | 1,118 |
| Originator | 721 | 885 |
| ACMP talker | 689 | 517 |
| MAAP | 519 | 267 |
| ADP | 442 | 471 |
| **Total** | **8,794** | **10,632** |

Those blocks also release 5 RAMB36 and 2 DSPs. Part of the 884-LUT timer service is freed as well.

What the fabric adds:
- the ingress filter and classifier: 300-600 LUT;
- four mailbox pairs: about 800 LUT and 4-8 RAMB18;
- the TX merge: about 200 LUT;
- the control registers firmware writes (talker licence, stream table, MAAP addresses): 200-400 LUT.

The total added is about **1,500-2,000 LUT, 1,500 FF and 4-8 RAMB18**. The net is about **-6,800 to -7,300 LUT** and **-9,000 FF**.

**Software side.** Estimated 25-40 KiB of code. The fixed 128 KiB ROM should hold it; measure the current use. RAM: 8-32 KiB, mostly the SRP attribute database. With D4 there is no DDR3, so this RAM comes from block RAM.

D5's smaller core must be re-checked for CPU load under SRP churn, with the ingress filter bounding it.

**Overlap with milestone 12.** M3 and M4 put ACMP, ADP and SRP on the shared sequencer, saving about 4,000 LUT in total. If milestone 13 later moves those blocks out of the fabric, that sequencer work on them is thrown away, and milestone 13's additional saving shrinks to about **-3,000 to -3,500 LUT**. A ruling is needed on how the two milestones divide this work.

[A10] **Owner, 2026-10-05:** the split architecture becomes Mark II's **default use case**. ADP, ACMP, MAAP and SRP run on the bare-metal core over the packet mailboxes, with fabric ingress filtering. The all-fabric build stays a supported option, and moving between the two must be easy. Placement is chosen per function at build time.

Still open, under discussion with the owner: whether it is integrated before the release (P3, milestone 6) or after it, and how the milestone 12 and 13 scopes are redrawn.

[A10] **Owner decision, 2026-10-05 12:58: the split lands before the release.** The software control plane (#665: ADP, ACMP, MAAP, SRP via lwSRP, AECP, and the saved-state handling; bare-metal first) is integrated in milestone 12, ahead of P3. #396's gate runs therefore run on the split image.

Each function ships in the split only after it passes its suites and the bench compliance re-run. Any other function ships all-fabric; the all-fabric build stays supported. Milestone 13 keeps the hard-core port.

**Consequences for the plan:**
- The shared-sequencer lanes M3 (ACMP/ADP part) and M4 are replaced by the split lanes F0-F5.
- The area lanes M2, M5, M6, M7 and M8 proceed after #661 merges.
- The plan document is revised to the split ledger before its PR.
- #664's requirement edits go to the owner for approval and must merge before any function's default placement changes.

[A10] **Round 1b of the Mark II plan** for [A540] (#640, stage 1). Branch `640-mark2-plan` at `06f5e7e5`, local and never published. The plan predates the decisions below. Reviewers: [R492] (internal) and [R493] (external), as in the stage-1 assignment.

1. **Merge dev `5603c353`** with a merge commit; no rebase. It brings the third pin adoption, F0-F4 of the bare-metal control plane, #686 and #645.
2. **Fold in every decision:**
   - the manager rulings [5990755268](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5990755268) (D1, D3, D6, D7, D8);
   - the owner decisions [5991591637](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991591637) (D2 no, D4 yes, D5 conditional, D9 no for Mark II);
   - the milestone 13 decisions [5991605450](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991605450), [5991626132](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991626132), [5991695093](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991695093) and [5991737927](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991737927);
   - the split as Mark II's default use case [5991745829](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991745829), landing before the release [5993114362](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5993114362).
3. **Re-baseline the ledger** on dev `5603c353`'s recorded endpoints (route-1x1, ooc-1x1, ooc-8x8 in the resource gate records; no new Vivado run is needed for the baseline). Add the split as a lever: what leaves the shipping image when the default flips (#664: after the F2-F5 bench), with a measured or clearly marked estimated LUT figure. Recompute the M-lane estimates against the 38,040 LUT bar (NFR-RES-01) with timing met.
4. **Lane table:** each of M2, M3, M5, M6, M7, M8, M10 (and M9, the re-record), with its scope, its dependency (pin, split flip or owner decision), its estimate and the order to run them.
5. Update `AREA_BUDGET.md` to match. Docs only; no RTL.

Post REVIEW READY with the head. The manager publishes the branch and opens the PR.

[A10] **Round 1c of the Mark II plan** for [A540] on PR #698, head `c4b8b7d3`. [R493-1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/698#issuecomment-6081524243) is POSITIVE. [R492-1](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/698#issuecomment-6081481326) is NEGATIVE on three MINORs.

1. **R492-1-F1: schedule the split-aware measurement (decision).** #665 lands everything behind a build switch whose default is the all-fabric placement. So the split placement can be measured without flipping the default. Name a lane, **M0s**, owned by the manager's resource bench, in two steps:
   - **now:** a split route with F0-F4 off the fabric and AECP still in fabric;
   - **after F5 merges:** the full split.
   Both come before the week-4 checkpoint and before the default flip. The D7 comparison uses M0s figures. The lane table, the "Lane sequence" text and AREA_BUDGET.md state the same order.
2. **R492-1-F2: M8a basis.** Describe the #649 figures as pre-packing LUT cells with the unowned remainder (`649_RESOURCE_MAP_AND_SENSITIVITY.md:262-273`). Then justify the 1,600 central figure and its range against that, or reprice it. Re-run `scripts/recompute_ledger.py` if any figure changes, and mirror the change in AREA_BUDGET.
3. **R492-1-F3: no-split and partial-flip scenarios.**
   - The no-split figure includes M3 and M10, or excludes them explicitly with the inclusive figure beside it.
   - Add a priced partial-flip scenario (F5 unqualified, AECP stays in fabric) with its assumptions.
   - State whether each scenario meets 38,040 and 37,659, and what extra lever or ruling it would need if not.
4. **Residue.** Shorten sentences where you touch text (R492-1-R1, R493-1-R1), and link references consistently (R493-1-R2). Anything left goes to the #495 checklist at merge.
5. **Suggestions adopted.** R492-1-S1: give the exact reproduction command for the L11b core pricing. R492-1-S2: name the SoC FIFOs that survive D4 in M2's scope.

Docs only. Commit on `c4b8b7d3` with no rebase or amend. Post REVIEW READY with the head.
